messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: subsetting AffymetrixCelSet and plotDensity
parts:
Hi,
So my assumption is that if I want to do some operation on a subset of
the arrays, say the first 5, I should do
as.list(cs)[1:5]
and hopefully the function exists with a .list method that knows this
and will operate on those arrays. At least, this seems to be the case
with plotDensity, though I'm not sure how universal this is.

But then I get the following error:

> plotDensity(as.list(csNTissue)[1:2])
Error in readCdfUnits(filename =
"annotationData/chipTypes/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2.cdf", :
Argument 'units' must be numeric or NULL: logical
> traceback()
15: stop("Argument 'units' must be numeric or NULL: ", class(units)[1])
14: readCdfUnits(filename =
"annotationData/chipTypes/HuEx-1_0-st-v2/HuEx-1_0-st-v2.cdf",
units = FALSE, stratifyBy = NULL)
13: do.call(.fcn, args = args)
12: doCall.default("readCdfUnits", filename = this$.pathname, units =
units,
...)
11: doCall("readCdfUnits", filename = this$.pathname, units = units,
...)
10: readUnits.AffymetrixCdfFile(getCdf(this), units = units, stratifyBy
= stratifyBy)
9: readUnits(getCdf(this), units = units, stratifyBy = stratifyBy)
8: withCallingHandlers(expr, warning = function(w)
invokeRestart("muffleWarning"))
7: suppressWarnings({
cdf <- readUnits(getCdf(this), units = units, stratifyBy =
stratifyBy)
})
6: readUnits.AffymetrixCelFile(this, units = units)
5: readUnits(this, units = units)
4: `[.AffymetrixCelFile`(x, is.finite(x))
3: x[is.finite(x)]
2: plotDensity.list(as.list(csNTissue)[1:2])
1: plotDensity(as.list(csNTissue)[1:2])
>

Is this a bug, or have I incorrectly subseted the arrays?
Best,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] subsetting AffymetrixCelSet and plotDensity
parts:
On Wed, Feb 20, 2008 at 1:50 PM, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi,
> So my assumption is that if I want to do some operation on a subset of
> the arrays, say the first 5, I should do
> as.list(cs)[1:5]
> and hopefully the function exists with a .list method that knows this
> and will operate on those arrays. At least, this seems to be the case
> with plotDensity, though I'm not sure how universal this is.

No, the plotDensity() for the 'list' class is in aroma.light, which
knows nothing about lists of AffymetrixCelFile:s. Consider as.list()
as a part of the API that is for developers only.

Instead, extract a sub-AffymetrixCelSet as follows:

cs2 <- extract(cs, 1:5)

and treat it as any other AffymetrixCelSet, e.g.

plotDensity(cs2)

Hope this helps

Henrik
